notes: SpaceX 10-Q cover (Jul 28, 2026): 7,696,293,669 A + 5,485,486,276 B, plus 391,041,680 A issued in the Cursor merger (8-K Aug 14). Not a company-reported total.

Derived. 424B4 beneficial ownership: Musk holds 849,494,440 A + 5,569,053,075 B (84.4% of votes, counting about 350M option shares). Outstanding-basis votes are about 10 x 5.219B B + 0.849B A ≈ 53.04B of about 62.94B total, which is ~84.3% and matches the 424B4 figure.
Schedule 13G/A filed Jun 16, 2026: 699,580,882 shares with voting rights. Excludes 423.7M award shares voted proportionally by proxy.
deal_math.parity_note: 1:1 market-cap parity works out to about $424 per TSLA at current prices (+24%), which clears the $450 floor.
deal_math.collar_note: An all-stock deal at a fixed ratio leaves Tesla holders exposed if SPCX falls before the vote. To win an independent Tesla vote it likely needs downside protection (a collar or price floor). SpaceX holders would resist, because it shifts value to Tesla holders if SPCX drops. This is general M&A practice, not deal-specific.
deal_math.reverse_note: Reverse case: Tesla acquires SpaceX. Tesla has one class of stock, so Musk's dual-class control would end. Shown for completeness; low probability.

fcc.note: The SpaceX-Grain transfer application was filed Oct 8 and asks for expedited consent. Its ECFS/ULS docket number wasn't found yet; the earlier T-Mobile to Grain proceeding was WT 25-178. The FCC's informal goal is 180 days for transaction review (general practice).

why: On SpaceX's Oct 20 earnings call, Musk said the Tesla and SpaceX boards have each formed a special committee of independent directors to look at a merger. He called it a good idea but said no terms are agreed and there's no guarantee.

Tesla's DEF 14A (Oct 19) still set a routine Dec 3 meeting with no merger item, so any deal goes the normal route: committee talks, fairness opinions, an S-4, then a separate announcement and a special meeting, most likely in 2027. Tesla needs 50% of all outstanding shares to approve.
With committees confirmed, the rules model rises to 56% for a merger letter or agreement by Jun 30, 2027 (60% of the committee-adjusted merger odds). That is a judgment call, not data.

Prediction markets price it at 55% on the volume-weighted Kalshi and Polymarket composite. Markets often move before the news hits the wire, so they get 40% of the weight. Dashboard number: 60% x 55.6% + 40% x 55.3% = 55.5%.

Catalysts to watch: Starship Flight 15 (NET Nov 20), the Nov 20 and Dec 18 monthly options expirations, the Dec 3 annual meeting Q&A, the Dec 8 SpaceX unlock, and any banker or law-firm hire by the committees. Unlock days and Starship launch days are less likely days for a deal letter.

kill.why: If a routine meeting is set with no SpaceX language, the 2026-meeting merger path is closed. Letter odds by mid-2027 are modeled as 0.6 x the pre-kill merger share: a clean routine proxy is evidence against a live deal, but a 2027 special meeting is still possible. This is judgment, not data. For comparison, Polymarket's Jun 30, 2027 contract is shown in details.

starship._why: NET Nov 8 comes from planning-grade sources: the CADENA air-traffic planning slides of Oct 8 (cited by Wikipedia), and NASASpaceflight reporting on Oct 10 plus Musk's '4-6 weeks' remark (per thelaunchwindow). SpaceX hasn't announced a date, and Launch Library lists it only as NET Q4 2026. Unverified. Merger odds: launch day x0.1 and the day after x0.3. After a success, days +2 to +4 get x1.3. After a failure, days +1 to +5 get x0.2. The status comes from data/events_state.json (set by watch.py or by hand) or from this config.
starship.evidence: Oct 26 23:11 ET tracker 'success' was a false positive: headlines were about Booster 22's Oct 25 static fire (Space.com, Aviation Week). Flight 15 still NET Nov 8, unflown.

grain._why: SpaceX agreed on Oct 8, 2026 to buy Grain's 800 MHz licenses, pending FCC consent. While it's pending, merger odds in the next 14 days get x0.9 (a soft reason to sequence the deal after approval). On approval, the following 5 days get x1.2. Each run checks ECFS (Grain/SpaceX filers, proceeding 25-178) and Google News for approval wording. Detection is heuristic, so confirm by hand.

docs._doc: Used once the state is meeting_only (Dec 3 AGM set, routine). Headline = merger letter (or definitive agreement) by `by`, conditional on none so far. Dashboard number = (1 - market_weight) x rules model + market_weight x market composite, plus any smart-money nudge.
docs._rules_why: Rules model: 0.6 x the pre-proxy merger share (letter_after_kill). With the committee signal on (Oct 20: both boards formed special committees), that share is 94%, so the rules number is 0.6 x 0.94 = 56%. The 0.6 keeps a haircut because Musk said no terms are agreed, there's no guarantee, and the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares. Judgment, not data.
docs._month_why: How the rules model spreads the letter odds over time. Spread fairly evenly, with a bit more weight in Dec (AGM Q&A, Day-180 unlock) and Feb (after SpaceX's Q4 results). Then multiplied by catalyst-day weights below. Oct 22, 2026: shifted 11 pts of weight from Oct-Dec 2026 into Jan-Jun 2027 after Bloomberg ('people familiar') said an announcement is targeted for the first half of 2027 and Reuters (person with direct knowledge) said Musk's public comments could delay the process by several weeks and talks are at an early stage. Total letter odds by Jun 30, 2027 unchanged; judgment, not data.
docs._market_why: Share of the dashboard number taken from the prediction-market composite. Markets often move before the news hits the wire, so they get real weight, but they are thin (a few $K a day), so not all of it.
docs.market: Composite: every live Kalshi (definitive agreement before X) and Polymarket (announced by X) contract is treated as the same event. A volume-weighted monotone fit is drawn through them (weight = 24h volume, at least min_vol_weight). Polymarket 'announced' can include a non-binding letter, Kalshi needs a definitive agreement, so the two are not identical; the fit splits the difference.
docs.smart_money: Flag 'Market moved before news': a contract moves 5+ pts in 24h with at least $1K traded and no filing or strict-filtered deal headline in that window. Nudge: if a flagged-quality move is 10+ pts within 72h, the dashboard adds 25% of that move (capped at 4 pts) on top of the blend, until news explains it or the move ages out.
